review_text_raw:
Well for a "Phone Simulator" it aint a bad game. Actually I enjoyed the story a lot but there were also a couple things I didnt like.

[spoiler]The first and only timed event is a bit harsh...theres a lot of talking that you needa read before you can actually react. When you finally have control over what happens they ask you to input things that you are not familiar with at this point of the story. Yes you can know them but youre not that far into it at this point to "know" them to enter those words within 30 seconds.
Another point I didnt like is that sometimes your choice really isnt clear enough. I knew exactly what I would do in specific situations and Im presented with choices that I cant really make sense of. Sometimes the outcome went into a different direction than I intended.
Last points are about the ending. Of course I got an ending I didnt like. I saved one and sacrificed another. Im not clear as to what the entity was referring with if things went differently I could have changed its mind and Im not playing through  this again to find out. Also during the last conversations I unlocked a vlog entry and got a couple chat messages...I was unable to actually read or view them since the final conversation...well youre locked in it.[/spoiler]

Technically I had three problems with it. First when I started it I got a black screen. Im running Win10 and had to run it in Win7 compatibility mode with fullscreen optimizations disabled. Than I had no sound because for some reason it automatically switched to my turned off headset. After fixing that I could play the whole game without problems. After the credits it went to black screen again so i hadt to alt+f4 it.

Anyway...story is great if you like to read...if you like adventures with not too hard riddles...go for it...the price is cheap for the hours of entertainment that you get.

review_text_raw:
Okay, so I'm a massive fan of "Sara Is Missing" which is no longer on Steam (presumably for the extreme content) which was one of the first games Kaigan Games released based on this series, I was excited to play this as I didn't realise this game was made from the same developers, I was extremely impressed! The content isn't as extreme as SIM because I think just about anyone can say that it was extremely dark and disturbing, but I think they were trialling how a game like SIM would do, and it was successful!

Enough about SIM, Simulacra is a fantastic game! The jumpscares are timed amazingly, allowing the player to calm before the next one when they least expect it. Unlike some other games when they over exaggerate the scariness. [spoiler] (I won't lie, I jumped massively at the phone reset and Taylor's jumpscare. That was cruel haha) [/spoiler] The characters are comical, [spoiler] Especially Greg with his voice notes LMFAO[/spoiler] They all have their own individual wittiness about them, personalities and not at any point did I feel like they were lack luster, they all contributed their own to the story which I really appreciate as I find a lot of horror games tend to make characters to make the player build up a connection only them to kill them in the middle or nearer towards the end.

The only critique I'd say would be the crashing, don't get me wrong! It happens to a lot of games, but I think more frequent saving should be happening or let the player save their progress manually in case it does happen. It doesn't happen often, but on the odd occasion I've needed to restart the game. Other than that, if you like a scare, thrill and a mystery; This game is for you. Plus, it's super cheap! Try it out!

review_text_raw: I love games with this sort of conceit, and really had a fun time with this! I love games where the devs clearly really enjoy the project and have a passion for it, it's so refreshing. While I did enjoy this (the others aren't optimized for Steam Deck and the second is unsupported so I might have to wait to play the rest), I do have a few mild quibbles. First, the game could use a brief refresh as far as the writing -- the localization for English was iffy, and while I can ignore some grammar/misspellings with no problem, this did impact the gameplay in a few instances. Also, and I know this is the result of playing on a Steam Deck but it did say it was optimized and entering the text was a pain and very easily the one thing I disliked. I couldn't do the "timed section text entry" (if you know you know) not because I didn't know the answers (I did), but the entry was just so fiddly. Honestly those are really mild complaints, but the localization issues made the end a little hard to follow. But like I said, it's very minor as the game was enjoyable despite that. Hoping the rest come to Steam Deck soon, and hoping the devs keep making fun, unique games like this!

I really enjoyed this game. From the moment i started playing i was hooked on the story & what was going to happen next. 
I like hacking & decoding the messages to gain clues to help me further in the game. I am not the biggest fan of the picture puzzles however that is just my personal opinion & you do get the option to skip those as well as the messages after a few attempts.
I like there is multiple ending & I enjoyed finding out how each one impacted the story. I like how the story left you thinking of the game & its meaning.
I will say the voice acting of the characters especially greg was cringy.
The jump scares are nice and well timed out through out the game & keeps you on edge as well as the visuals in the background e.g. lights flickering. The audio is good and i enjoyed the random breathing noises etc that happened when you did certain things.
I would defo recommend this to anyone who is a horror fan & story based game fan. I am looking forward to playing the second one.
